leakage_findings.issue: Sub-target aggregates group by (jurisdiction, period_id) and average the target across train rows for other overdose_category values at the same (jurisdiction, period_id) cell. For a given val row with category X at (jur, pid), the fold-train rows for that same (jur, pid) exist only if pid falls in the fold's train period set — for forward-expanding CV this is always true (val pid > all train pids), so the (jur, pid) cell in fold-train is EMPTY. The pipeline falls back to the fold-train global mean, making these features constant within each fold's val set. They carry zero information in OOF but non-zero information at inference (where full-train cross-category data exists), creating a train/OOF representation mismatch. Not classical leakage (no future target used), but the OOF representation differs from inference representation.
leakage_findings.required_fix: Group subtgt_mean_* by (jurisdiction, period_id_lag1) — i.e., use the prior period's cross-category mean — so the same look-back window is available in both train and val rows. Alternatively drop these and replace with target_lag1 broken out per category (already captured by target_lag1/lag3/lag6 which are correctly computed).

leakage_findings.feature: imputation medians (juris_train_medians, global_train_medians) for unemployment_rate, labor_force, temp_avg_f, precip_in
leakage_findings.issue: Jurisdiction-level and global medians are computed once on the full training frame (lines 198-199 of feature_pipeline.py) before the CV split and applied to both train and pred. For the train set this means fold-val rows' missing covariate values are imputed using statistics that include fold-val data. This is a low-risk issue since these are exogenous covariates (not target-derived), but it constitutes a mild fold-unsafe imputation.
leakage_findings.required_fix: Compute jurisdiction medians inside the per-fold loop on fold_train rows only, then apply to val rows. The full-train medians for pred imputation remain correct as-is.

leakage_findings.issue: Image SVD is fit on ALL unique train images at once (line 940-943: img_svd.fit(gray_arr) where gray_arr covers all train keys). The image sidecar is a static, non-target-derived observation so this is NOT target leakage. However the SVD basis is fit on the same set used for evaluation, which for a small number of unique images (jurisdiction x period) may overfit the image manifold. Since delta=+0.001836 is small and positive, this is low risk.
leakage_findings.required_fix: No fix required for correctness; acceptable per audit rules for static image features. Noted for completeness.

suggestions.suggestion: Build on period_id__ordinal_rank and target_lag1 (top contributors per datetime_derived delta=0.017 and other_features delta=0.0014): add interaction target_lag1 * period_id__ordinal_rank and target_lag1 / (tgt_mean_jur_cat + 1e-6) to capture trend-relative-to-group deviation, computed inside the per-fold lag loop.
suggestions.implementation_hint: After computing target_lag1 OOF inside fold loop, compute ratio_lag1_to_jur_cat = target_lag1 / (tgt_mean_jur_cat + 1e-6) and trend_x_lag = target_lag1 * period_id__ordinal_rank per fold val rows; apply same formula at inference using full-train values.

suggestions.suggestion: Replace subtgt_mean_* (mismatch between OOF and inference) with cross-category lag features: for each sub-target category c, compute subtgt_lag1_c = the target value at (jurisdiction, period_id_rank-1) for category c, using full-train sorted data. This preserves the cross-category signal without the (jur, pid) emptiness problem in OOF.
suggestions.implementation_hint: In the per-fold loop, for each sub-cat c: filter fold_train to rows where overdose_category==c, sort by (jurisdiction, period_rank), shift(1) grouped by jurisdiction, then join to val rows on (jurisdiction, period_rank-1). For pred, use full-train shift(1) from last train period.

suggestions.suggestion: text_svd group was correctly pruned (delta=-0.000853, decision=prune). Confirm it remains absent. No other groups fall clearly into prune territory but per_fold_aggregates shows delta=-0.009177 (removal lowers MAE); do not expand this group further.
suggestions.implementation_hint: text_svd_0 through text_svd_7 already in ablation_pruned_columns; verify specialist feature list excludes them — confirmed in agent_gbdt.json authored_features_used.

suggestions.suggestion: Add target_roll12_mean / target_roll3_mean ratio (acceleration proxy) and target_lag1 - target_lag3 (short-term momentum) as new features within the existing per-fold lag loop, leveraging already-computed lag values.
suggestions.implementation_hint: After computing target_roll3_mean and target_roll12_mean OOF, add roll_accel = target_roll3_mean / (target_roll12_mean + 1e-6) and tgt_momentum = target_lag1 - target_lag3 as derived columns in the same fold loop iteration.

notes: No HIGH-severity leakage found. CV uses forward-expanding canonical folds correctly; all target aggregates (tgt_mean_*, te_*, tgt_mean_gtrends_*) confirmed fit per fold on fold-train rows only (not ~val_mask). subtgt_mean_* features have a train/OOF representation mismatch (empty cell fallback) warranting replacement. Image SVD fit on full train is safe for static sidecar. text_svd correctly pruned. Imputation medians are computed globally — minor fold-unsafety for exogenous covariates only.
